There is a category of knowledge that accumulates as you work and never makes it
into a paper: why that mixed model will not converge, how to actually read a
periodogram, what `scale()` does to your coefficients, the least painful way to
plot confidence intervals. This blog is for that.

## What I will write about

- **R and the tidyverse** — patterns I use every day, and the ones I abandoned.
- **Applied statistics** — inference, mixed models, periodic data analysis, and
  the misunderstandings I see repeated in practice.
- **Visualisation** — `ggplot2`, design decisions, and plots that communicate.
- **Workflow** — reproducible projects, Quarto, version control.

The aim is for each post to be short, self-contained, and to carry code you can
copy and run.

## How this site is built

The site is written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and published with GitHub
Pages. Every post is a `.qmd` file, so text and code live together and results
are generated at render time:

```r
library(tidyverse)

# An example of what tends to show up around here
tibble(t = seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(signal = sin(t) + rnorm(n(), sd = 0.2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(t, signal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "#1d6a73") +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "Signal") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

One advantage of this setup: results are *frozen* (`freeze: true`), so the server
that publishes the site does not need R installed. Code runs only when I change
a post.
